entries.note: “Probably” qualifies an evaluative ranking of LLM problems.

entries.test: Public Sora outputs would show whether it generates factual or structural errors such as malformed chessboards.
entries.note: In context, “makes things up” means errors in depicted reality.

entries.test: Public LLM responses and the referenced Sora video would show confidently presented factual errors and the depicted chessboard's defects.
entries.note: He adopts the quoted expression himself. The proposition broadens a comparison about one Sora image into a frequency claim about Sora output generally.

entries.test: Public tests of Sora's chess depictions would show whether it reliably respects standard board dimensions and chess rules.
entries.note: The surrounding examples give “clueless about chess” a concrete capability reading.

entries.test: Published controlled experiments varying Sora's compute while holding other factors fixed would test whether inadequate compute explains the chessboard error.
entries.note: A causal mechanism is empirically testable even if the necessary experiments have not been published.

entries.test: Public compute disclosures and controlled scaling experiments would test whether Sora's chessboard errors are attributable to insufficient compute.
entries.note: The preceding paragraph supplies the stated compute premise.

entries.test: Public multimodal model evaluations and outputs would establish whether hallucinations and additional visual errors persist.
Sora's published training description and the referenced chess video would establish whether video-text grounding coexists with the specified chessboard errors.
entries.note: The claim concerns the insufficiency of grounding in Sora, not every possible grounded system.
The proposition preserves the explicit “probably” qualification.
“Not a direct function” does not distinguish copying, statistical dependence, or causal dependence clearly enough for a shared test.

entries.test: The referenced chess output and public evidence of chess examples in Sora's training data would test the claimed failure despite ample relevant evidence.
entries.note: The source identifies a particular cultural regularity; the proposition generalizes to cultural regularities broadly.

entries.test: The referenced output and disclosed training examples would test whether Sora generated a novel chess scene while violating standard chessboard constraints.
entries.note: The source discusses the wrong generalization in this example and calls generalization “arguably” present. The proposition broadens and firms up those commitments.

entries.test: Published architecture analyses, representation studies, and controlled evaluations would test whether Sora lacks physical and cultural models and whether that explains its world-depiction errors.
entries.note: The proposition changes “does not try to build” internal models into their actual absence. Its explicit explanatory “because” makes it causal.

entries.test: Public tests of scene-wide consistency and object persistence, alongside representation analyses, would test the claimed absence of global scene comprehension.
entries.note: The added statement about outputs removes the source's restriction to most or all observed errors and its “virtually every bit” qualification.

entries.test: Public technical documentation and studies of Sora's internal representations would test whether its mechanism relies on local pixel reconstruction without whole-object representations.
entries.note: The metaphor conveys a substantive claim about the model's mechanism.
“Immense warning sign” evaluates significance without specifying an AGI outcome.

entries.test: Public Sora outputs, architecture documentation, and training-data disclosures would establish whether factual errors persist in the described architecture at large data scale.

entries.note: This recommends earlier recognition of the preceding problems.

entries.test: Public evaluations of world modeling, high-level reasoning, and factual accuracy across generative models with increasing training-data scale would test the claimed persistent difficulties.
entries.note: The third-person self-reference remains Marcus's own assertion.

entries.test: The Sora samples public by February 17, 2024 would establish the proportion dominated by smooth pans and slow motion, while technical studies could test reliance on local patches.
entries.note: Marcus adopts the observation while crediting others. “Most” weakens “the vast majority,” and the mechanism remains a suggestion rather than an established finding.
